Q0186

“Whence has it all the materials of reason and knowledge? To this…” — John Locke (Q0186)

An English quotation associated with An Essay Concerning Human Understanding, II.i.2, organized here under experience.

Quotes / John Locke / Q0186

English

Whence has it all the materials of reason and knowledge? To this I answer, in one word, from experience.
Thinker John Locke
School British Empiricism
Source An Essay Concerning Human Understanding, II.i.2
Theme Experience
Another quotation More from this thinker

Context and commentary are editorial aids for reading. They do not replace the primary text or scholarly commentary.

Source context

Archive record: this English passage is associated with An Essay Concerning Human Understanding, II.i.2, within the British Empiricism tradition. Use the cited work or edition when a scholarly attribution is needed.

A short reading

Read in the register of experience, the sentence asks the reader to test an assumption rather than to collect a slogan. In John Locke's wider work, similar claims are usually offered as prompts for judgment: what would have to be true for the sentence to hold, and what would follow if it did?
